items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: I had a really good trumpet teacher in high school named Sidney Baker

ctx.x: Oh yeah. I grew up listening to all that music. Well hearing it. I was hearing it in the background ‘cause I had family members that really loved that stuff. But at that time, in 1975, I was at the time, I started out at the High School of Music & Art. I was a freshman at that time, and I was discovering Charlie Parker and Dizzy and Freddie Hubbard. That’s what I was getting into. I was also really into classical music so I was discovering some

wonderful recordings like there’s a recording of the Philadelphia, New York, and I want to say Chicago Symphony brass sections playing the Gabrieli Canzon. It was a very famous recording that was put out by I want to say RCA. And I had a really good trumpet teacher in high school named Sidney Baker who was from that tradition. So you just, when you’re around it that’s what you know. And mind you, this is before the Internet. So if you wanted to really seek out information you had to really put some — you had to…
It’s okay, we are doing home studio today.
